# Chess Engine

An algorithmic chess engine written in Python, built one measured step at a time,
and playable right in the browser.

> **Headline (filled in by the benchmark harness, never by hand):**
> Estimated Elo went from **`1075` → `???`** through move ordering, quiescence search,
> iterative deepening, transposition tables and positional evaluation.

## What this project shows

- **Search:** negamax with alpha-beta pruning, move ordering (MVV-LVA, killers),
  quiescence search, iterative deepening under a time limit, and a Zobrist-hashed
  transposition table.
- **Evaluation:** material, piece-square tables with middlegame/endgame tapering, and a
  few chosen pawn-structure terms.
- **Measurement:** every engine version is tagged and run through the same harness, which
  records nodes, speed, tactical-suite score and **estimated Elo** with error bars. Each
  feature's README claim is backed by recorded data.
- **Playable anywhere:** a stateless Flask API runs as a Vercel serverless function
  (free, about a second to start), and the board page embeds directly in a portfolio site.

## Project layout (target)

```
engine/        # the engine itself (pure Python, depends only on python-chess)
  evaluation.py
  search.py
  uci.py       # UCI protocol, so the engine can play in GUIs and in rating matches
harness/       # telemetry and Elo estimation (see docs/BENCHMARKING.md)
api/           # Flask app, deployed as a Vercel serverless function
web/           # static board page served by Vercel
telemetry/     # recorded results (results.jsonl), committed to the repo
tests/
docs/
```
